final_proof:
Let $\mathbb{Z}_p$ be the set of $p$-adic integers, which is defined as the valuation ring associated with the $p$-adic norm on $\mathbb{Q}_p$, i.e., $\mathbb{Z}_p = \{ x \in \mathbb{Q}_p : \|x\|_p \le 1 \}$.

First, we determine the non-units of $\mathbb{Z}_p$. An element $x \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ is a unit if and only if there exists $y \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ such that $xy = 1$. This implies $\|x\|_p \|y\|_p = \|1\|_p = 1$. Since $\|x\|_p \le 1$ and $\|y\|_p \le 1$, this requires $\|x\|_p = 1$. Therefore, the set of non-units in $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is exactly $M = \{ x \in \mathbb{Z}_p : \|x\|_p < 1 \}$.

The values of the $p$-adic norm on $\mathbb{Q}_p \setminus \{0\}$ are integer powers of $p$. Thus, if $\|x\|_p < 1$, we must have $\|x\|_p \le 1/p$. 
This means $x \in M \iff \|x\|_p \le 1/p$.

Notice that $\|p\|_p = 1/p$. We can write any $x \in M$ as $x = p(x/p)$. Then $\|x/p\|_p = p\|x\|_p \le 1$, meaning $x/p \in \mathbb{Z}_p$. 
Thus, any $x \in M$ belongs to the principal ideal $p\mathbb{Z}_p$. Conversely, if $x = py \in p\mathbb{Z}_p$ for $y \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, then $\|x\|_p = \|p\|_p \|y\|_p \le 1/p < 1$, so $x \in M$. 
Hence, $M = p\mathbb{Z}_p$, which is an ideal (as it is generated by a single element).

In a commutative ring with identity, if the set of all non-units forms an ideal, then this ideal is the unique maximal ideal, and the ring is a local ring. 
Since $M = p\mathbb{Z}_p$ is exactly the set of all non-units and it is an ideal, it follows that $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is a local ring (proving a) and $p\mathbb{Z}_p$ is its unique maximal ideal (proving b).
